messages:
nina: FYI customer hit a double-charge from a streaming request that did a tool call during a reconnect. happened on canary. trace=pp-3c2b

omar: double-charge how? provisional + confirmed or duplicate confirmed?

nina: provisional optimistic charge written when router accepted the session, then runtime retried the toolcall after a route swap and emitted a confirmed charge. no dedupe happened. logs:```\n[pp-3c2b] router: accept, provisional_est=140 tokens, session_hint=model-xl\n[pp-3c2b] route swap -> region-lowcost (headers rewritten)\n[pp-3c2b] runtime: toolcall replayed, tool_id=null, tokens_used=102\n[pp-3c2b] billing: confirmed+102 tokens\n```\n
lee: do we not include the client's idempotency header in the runtime request?

nina: client sent idempotency-id, router lost it when rewriting headers to comply with internal routing. so runtime saw no idempotency.

ciara: hmm two axes: header-preservation bug + billing model that charges provisional immediately. we should avoid final invoice surprises.

billing-bot: note: current ledger flow: provisional entries are marked as provisional_tag and are 'applied' immediately to customer balance. confirmed entries are additive; we rely on dedupe by runtime_request_id to avoid duplicates.

omar: proposal: use a stable session_commit_id generated at router ingress and attach to all downstream writes (provisional and confirmed). billing dedupe should join on session_commit_id first, then runtime_request_id.

lee: +1. also need rule for model swaps: provisional estimates come from model_profile.estimate_tokens(model_hint). when fallback to smaller model yields lower tokens, we must ensure final charge replaces provisional instead of adding.

ciara: simpler semantics: provisional = not yet invoiced, show in console as pending. when confirmed arrives, replace pending with confirmed. only if confirmed never arrives (TTL) do we auto-expire pending and create a follow-up adjustment ticket. this avoids heuristics in ledger math.

billing-bot: that requires changing 'applied' behavior for provisional entries. will need migration: separate bucket 'pending_balance' vs 'invoiced_balance'.

omar: telemetry: emit events billing.pending.created(session_commit_id, estimate, model_hint), billing.finalized(session_commit_id, confirmed_tokens), billing.pending.expired(session_commit_id). hook these into observability join key session_commit_id. also surface delta metric: pending->final delta pct.

lee: internal API debate: should router own session_commit_id generation or runtime? router sees initial client headers and is the only stable handoff across reroutes. runtime would have to accept and validate header. downside: router couples to billing but easier for dedupe.

ciara: I vote router emits X-Session-Commit and we treat it as optional; if absent runtime synthesizes one and billing tags as runtime-scoped. router change must preserve all client idempotency headers untouched unless explicitly rewritten.

nina: short-term mitigation: revert the header-rewrite rule in canary and add a runtime guard that rejects toolcall replay if no idempotency header present (fail fast).

ops-bot: alert created: "provisional_vs_confirmed_delta" crossing 7% in last 10m for org=customer-xyz.

lee: console work: show pending bucket separate from invoiced, tooltip "pending may be adjusted on finalization", link to support flow. add an admin flag to surface large pending items for manual review.

omar: PRs/owners: router#102 preserve-idempotency-headers (sara), billing#523 pending-ledger (alyssa), console#344 pending-ui (lee), telemetry#210 session-commit-events (omar).

ciara: QA: test scenarios: network-reconnect + route-swap, client retry with idempotency header intact, client retry when header lost, model fallback with lower tokenization, truncated stream EOF vs early reconnect. create harness cases.

nina: thanks. if we agree I'll open the design doc for billing pending semantics and a small canary to start with router-preserve-headers revert. ping when tasks are in flight. :thumbsup:
